searchText: Hey <@!848401002108682261> please do not post the same comments across multiple channels/servers. Give time for people to answer your question and if it isn't getting answered try a different venue (Reddit, Twitter, etc.) still didn't answer the question. no one person hosts the chain, every node hosts a copy of it. > who is hosting the chain? Everyone is. Every user of Ethereum has a full copy of the entire database and runs the entire execution environment. no someone has the lead node.... There is no leader, there is no authority. the block count comes from the one person giving out the slot numbers...................................... All clients on the network are equal to each other, no one has any preferential treatment. the block count is automated... ? Blocks are currently produced by a "game" (proof of work). The game takes about 14 seconds on average to play and the winner is the first person to solve a particular puzzle. yes it is automation the blocks are blank Anyone can participate in this game (mining), and the winner is different each round. then validator validates the slot the blocks are assigned numbers an the they are filled with transactions I think <@!848401002108682261> is talking about the Beacon Chain. but idk If you are talking about proof of stake, there is a selection system for deciding who is next. Look for articles on RANDAO for details. notice how RPC went to gRPC i had to host the chain on the cloud You can run your client wherever you like. On a computer at home, or in the cloud, or you can outsource hosting to a third party. Everyone who uses Ethereum and/or participates in consensus has a similar choice. beacon chain is being mined by eth1 miners look at a tx score yes, you can host a node on cloud services, but that doesn't mean someone controls the block numbers its slot number produces 10 blocks per slot i have a node that is counting out the slots then its handed over to validation aka eth1 miners for block registry. go check eth1 miner mining beacon chaoin blocks eth1 miners are giving out the block numbers for beacon chain does that mean they are already intergraded? beaconcha.in is where u can view the eth1 deposit via MV3 something is wrong with etherscan.io an beaconscan.com
